_comment: Expectations for `gnd validate v2_expense.orm.yaml --trace`. --trace is the SHIPPED PRODUCER of operations_digest, which every steps.json is required to carry, which is why the size cut that would have dropped it was withdrawn.

other_paths.name: trace-over-a-v1-model
other_paths.story: A v1 document declares no operations, so --trace has nothing to compile and no fact type to grade. It must still exit 0 and still print both digests -- operations_digest over an absent section is the digest of [], which is the value a steps.json for a v1 model would have to carry.

other_paths.name: trace-over-invalid-model
other_paths.story: --trace never reaches compilation if layer 2 rejects the model. Reporting on a model that does not load would be reporting on nothing.

compiled.why: literal-free single atom whose `expense` parameter is also bound by the assert of expense_reimbursed
same shape, deontic -- the only route to finding class 8's warning half

compilation_rule_note: Q8: the rule reads 'a literal-free single-atom precondition WHOSE PARAMETER is also a parameter of an asserted fact type' and does not quantify. pre_submitted binds TWO parameters -- $expense (bound by the assert) and $submission (bound by nothing). This fixture assumes the existential reading (at least one). Under a universal reading pre_submitted does NOT compile, the corpus has no alethic compiled obligation at all, and reimburse-unsubmitted becomes unpinnable. The quantifier needs stating normatively.

transition_only.reason: literal binding on the status role
literal binding on the status role
two atoms, and a literal binding on the status role
two atoms, and a literal binding on the status role

frame_modality_note: Per-fact-type grading over the WHOLE model here, not over a walk: a fact type touched by ANY deontic-framed operation grades deontic. expense_has_status and expense_submitted_to_workday are both touched by the deontic-framed submit_expense_to_workday. In a walk that does not use that operation they grade alethic -- which is exactly why sneaky-side-effect (approve only) fails at 1 while audit-log-drift (approve + submit) warns. The harness must compute this per walk.

model_warnings.note: threshold_only_increases takes a subject its own effects never touch, so it can never fire. Owner decision 2026-08-20 (ledger 14): the evaluator stays silent and layer 2 says so at authoring time. Exactly one operation in this model trips the rule.
